title: gci settings
description: The whole of gci's configuration, at .gci/settings.json under the project root. It is read on every call, so an edit lands without a restart.

$schema.description: This schema, for an editor's completion and checks. gci ignores it.

deny.description: What no tool reads, writes or syncs. Not a sandbox: the client's own tools answer to its own permissions, so a file that must stay unread needs the same globs there too.

protect.description: What tools may read but never change. .gci/, .mcp.json, .claude/, every .git/ and gci's own package (when it lives in the tree) are always protected, besides these.

skip.description: Directory and file names a recursive walk does not enter. A path that names one directly still works.

tmp.description: The scratch directory, relative to the root: temporary files and run logs (under gci/logs/). It never travels in a sync, and should be in .gitignore.

max_output.description: The most characters one tool result may hold. A script's output past it is cut from the middle, keeping more of the end, with a pointer to its log.

edit_self.description: Lift the protection from gci's own package, for the repo that develops it.

vars.description: Vars every script can use as {name} in an argument, cwd, env or path value, beside the built-ins: python, exe, tmp, root, platform, home. A var may use the built-ins and the vars before it.

oneOf.description: A value per platform (macos, windows, linux, or a sys.platform prefix), with an optional "default" for the rest.

env.description: Environment variables set for every script, beneath each script's own.

path.description: Directories put ahead of PATH for every script, after each script's own.

defaults.description: Defaults for every script, beneath each script's own keys of the same names, for whatever a caller leaves out.

scripts.description: The scripts run_script can run, by name. Only these run: an agent cannot run a command a person did not write here.

globs.description: Globs: one without a / matches a name at any depth (.env); one with a / the root-relative path (secrets/**, everything under secrets/).

argv.description: A program and its arguments, run as given, with no shell (write ["sh", "-c", "..."] for one). An argument that is exactly {args} is where a caller's arguments go.

defaultHosts.description: run_script's hosts when the caller gives none: names from remote.hosts, and local for here. Unset, a run is here alone. A caller overrides it with ["local"].

defaultSync.description: Whether run_script syncs this tree to each host before running, when the caller does not say.

defaultWait.description: Seconds run_script waits before answering with the output so far and a job id, leaving the run going (MCP only; on the command line a run is waited out). Unset, it waits the run out.

defaultGrep.description: A Python regex: run_script's answer keeps only the output lines matching it. The log keeps every line.

defaultAfter.description: Lines kept after each grep match, like grep -A: an error's detail.

defaultTail.description: Only the last N lines of the output (after grep).

defaultTimeout.description: Seconds before a run is killed with its whole process tree, shared by all of a script's commands. null or 0 for none.

script.description: A script: exactly one of command, commands, run or forbid. Each run_script default may be set here too, over the settings' defaults; null clears a shared one.

description.description: What the script is for, as the scripts tool lists it.

commands.description: Argvs run in order; the first that fails stops the script.

run.description: A gauntlet: other scripts by name, run in order with an OK/FAIL line each and the failing one's output, stopping at the first failure unless keep_going. A gauntlet cannot run another, and skips a member for another platform.

forbid.description: Regex rules checked over the files a sync would carry: a house-style lint with no code.

args.description: Whether a caller may add arguments, appended to the last command or put where {args} is. Never for run or forbid.

cwd.description: Where the commands run, relative to the root.

env.description: Environment variables for this script, over the settings' own.

path.description: Directories put ahead of PATH for this script, before the settings' own.

platforms.description: The only platforms it runs on: macos, windows, linux, or a sys.platform prefix. Elsewhere a direct call refuses it and a gauntlet skips it.

keep_going.description: For run: carry on past a failing member, reporting every one.

files.description: For forbid: only the files matching these.

exclude.description: For forbid: not the files matching these.

pattern.description: A Python regex, multiline: ^ and $ match at every line.

message.description: What a match is reported as; the pattern itself if unset.

remote.description: Other machines that run the scripts. Files are edited here; each host runs `gci serve` in its own checkout, and a run there syncs this tree to it first.

hosts.description: Host names to addresses (on port) or URLs. An agent reaches only the hosts named here.

port.description: The port of a host given as an address, and the one `gci serve` listens on.

key_env.description: The environment variable holding the shared API key every request carries. The key belongs in neither the settings nor the tree, since both travel.

key_file.description: The file holding the API key when key_env is unset.

ignore.description: Lines in gitignore syntax a sync leaves out, after the root .gitignore's.
